title: Impact of AI-assisted microlearning on student engagement in an online environment in higher education
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether AI-assisted microlearning can improve student engagement in an online higher-education course. The authors focus on the problem that traditional online microlearning is often static and non-adaptive, while generative AI may enable personalized, bite-sized learning experiences that better sustain attention, participation, and motivation.

The intervention was implemented in a multimedia course in the Technology Education department at Palestine Technical University–Kadoorie. The experimental condition used AI-assisted microlearning modules supported by tools such as ChatGPT for generating quizzes and feedback, Canva AI for producing short instructional videos and visual materials, and adaptive learning elements such as quizzes, chatbots, and leaderboards. The comparison group received traditional online learning materials without AI personalization. The study used a quasi-experimental mixed-methods design with pre- and post-engagement measures plus forum comments and semi-structured interviews.

Participants were 50 pre-service teachers at the third- and fourth-year undergraduate level in Palestine. Quantitative results showed significant gains in overall engagement and in cognitive, behavioral, emotional, and social engagement for the AI-assisted group. Qualitative findings suggested that AI-assisted microlearning increased attention, reduced frustration, supported task completion, encouraged sharing and peer interaction, and made learning feel more personalized. The authors conclude that generative AI combined with microlearning can enhance engagement in online higher education, especially by strengthening cognitive engagement through adaptive and personalized content delivery.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental mixed-methods study with pre/post comparison and an ANCOVA, but it is not a true randomized controlled trial and uses a small single-site sample. The evidence is strengthened by qualitative triangulation, yet overall credibility is limited by design and generalizability concerns.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects on engagement are large in magnitude, especially for cognitive engagement, but the study population is narrow and the outcome is engagement rather than achievement. Given the size of the observed effects but limited external validity, the impact is modest-to-strong for the studied context rather than broadly generalizable.

interventions.use_case: AI-assisted microlearning for an online multimedia course, delivering bite-sized videos, infographics, quizzes, forums, and adaptive content personalized to learner performance and preferences
ChatGPT used to generate personalized quizzes and provide instant feedback and question-answer support within the microlearning workflow
Adaptive personalization of microlearning content, adjusting difficulty and recommending resources based on quiz results and interaction patterns
Gamified microlearning elements including leaderboards, badges, and point-based competition to increase participation and task completion

finding.finding_summary: AI-assisted microlearning significantly improved overall student engagement in a quasi-experimental study of n=50 college students (experimental n=25, control n=25). ANCOVA controlling for pre-test scores found a significant group effect on total engagement, F(1,47)=23.882, p<.001, with partial eta squared reported as 0.825 for total engagement; the authors interpreted this as a large impact. The intervention was also associated with reduced frustration, higher motivation, and greater comfort with learning activities.
finding.measure: Student engagement scale and qualitative interview/forum themes related to engagement, frustration, motivation, and attention

finding.finding_summary: The intervention improved multiple engagement-related durable skill dimensions, including cognitive, behavioral, emotional, and social engagement. Reported ANCOVA effects were significant for cognitive engagement, F(1,47)=47.171, partial eta squared=0.849; behavioral engagement, F(1,47)=12.215, partial eta squared=0.413; emotional engagement, F(1,47)=7.113, partial eta squared=0.634; and social engagement, F(1,47)=10.018, partial eta squared=0.327, all p<.001. Qualitative themes indicated gains in attention, personalized learning, task completion, sharing, and peer interaction.
finding.measure: Cognitive, behavioral, emotional, and social engagement subscales plus forum/interview coding

finding.finding_summary: The paper was situated in a multimedia course and reported that AI-assisted microlearning helped students understand course concepts, apply multimedia tools, and complete course tasks more effectively. However, the primary measured outcomes were engagement-related rather than direct achievement test scores, so any academic achievement inference is indirect and not tied to a standardized learning outcome.
finding.measure: Qualitative course-related understanding and task completion; no direct achievement test reported
